items.title: Paragraphs
items.text: Leave an empty line between paragraphs. Single line breaks are ignored, so wrap lines however you like.
items.code:
The storm had passed by morning.

Mara walked down to the harbour.

items.title: Italics and bold
items.text: Underscores make italics; stars make bold.

items.title: Quotes and dashes
items.text: Type plain quotes and Typst curls them. Two hyphens make an en dash, three an em dash.
items.code: "Come in," she said --- and closed the door. Pages 10--12.

items.title: A line break without a new paragraph
items.text: End the line with a backslash, as in poems or addresses.
items.code:
Roses are red, \
violets are blue.

items.title: Notes to yourself
items.text: Lines starting with // never appear in the book. Use /* … */ for longer notes.
items.code:
// TODO: check this date with the archive.
The ship sailed in 1820.

items.title: Characters with a special meaning
items.text: # * _ $ @ < \ and ` mean something to Typst. To write one as itself, put a backslash in front of it.

items.title: Chapters and sections
items.text: One = starts a chapter, == a section, === a subsection.
items.code:
= The Voyage
== Leaving port
=== The first night

items.title: Lists
items.text: A dash starts a bullet; a plus starts a numbered step.
items.code:
- salt
- flour

+ Mix the dry ingredients.
+ Add the water.

items.title: A new page
items.text: Force the next text onto a new page.

items.title: Adding a chapter file
items.text: Create a file in the chapters folder, then add an #include line for it in main.typ. Chapters appear in the order of these lines.

items.title: Footnotes
items.text: The note goes where you put it; Typst numbers it and places it at the bottom of the page.
items.code: The letter was never sent.#footnote[It is now in the county archive.]

items.title: Citing a source
items.text: Cite with @ and the source's key from your .bib file. The bibliography lists everything you cite.
items.code: As @smith2020 showed, the habit forms within weeks.

items.title: Pictures with captions
items.text: Put the image in your project (PNG, JPG or SVG). The <label> lets you refer to it elsewhere with @.
items.code:
#figure(
  image("figures/map.png", width: 80%),
  caption: [The island in 1820.],
) <fig-map>

The route is shown in @fig-map.

items.title: A longer quotation
items.text: Set a quotation apart from the text, with who said it.

items.title: Formulas
items.text: Dollar signs around math. With spaces inside, it gets its own line.
items.code:
The area is $pi r^2$.

$ x = (-b plus.minus sqrt(b^2 - 4 a c)) / (2 a) $

items.title: Red squiggles
items.text: They mark a Typst error. The usual cause is an unclosed *, _ or $, which turns the rest of the paragraph bold, italic or into math: close it, or put a backslash in front if you meant the character itself. Click the error count in the status bar to jump to the problem, or ask the assistant to fix it.

items.title: Ask the assistant
items.text: Select some text and press ⌘I, then ask anything: "How do I put this in two columns?", "Why is everything after this bold?" It can explain the markup or make the change for you.

shortcuts: Ask the assistant about the selection
